static_traits.name: Lin Na
static_traits.family_status: Lives with husband; husband will retire next year; no children
static_traits.social_status: Former students and colleagues often visit and offer support, but currently finds it hard to open up to them about troubles
static_traits.medical_history: No major physical illness; no psychotherapy or treatment related to psychological problems received; no similar psychological problems in the past career
static_traits.language_features: Expresses clearly, able to identify and describe repetitive negative thoughts; positive attitude, willing to cooperate

basic_info.main_problem: Because a former student did not visit as promised, I feel I am a useless teacher, leading to feelings of worthlessness and self-blame.
basic_info.core_demands: When these feelings of inadequacy began to affect my daily life and my enjoyment of retirement plans, I decided to seek counseling.
growth_experiences: Taught for a long time and has retired; during her career, many students thanked her and described her as 'dedicated and making learning interesting and meaningful', and many students performed well academically.
Photography hobby: after retirement, she used to carry a camera while walking to shoot; capturing beautiful moments makes her feel calm and accomplished.
Social support: former students and colleagues often visit and give support, but she currently finds it hard to open up to them about the present distress.

core_beliefs: I am not important, not valued by students

special_situations.event: A former student has not yet visited as promised
special_situations.conditional_assumptions: If students do not keep their commitments, it means I am not important and I am a failure as a teacher
special_situations.compensatory_strategies: Tries to rationalize and remind the self of the positive impact on other students, but inwardly still repeatedly self-blames
special_situations.automatic_thoughts: I am not a good teacher; they do not care about me

special_situations.event: Recalling interactions with former students or reflecting on one's teaching career
special_situations.conditional_assumptions: If students' affirmation and visit support cannot be continuously obtained, it proves I have no value
special_situations.compensatory_strategies: Repeatedly reviews past experiences, trying to find evidence to refute negative thoughts (cognitive reappraisal)
special_situations.automatic_thoughts: I have never truly influenced students

special_situations.event: Thinking about the life changes brought by the husband's upcoming retirement
special_situations.conditional_assumptions: If there is no clear role and others' need, my worth will decrease
special_situations.compensatory_strategies: Worries in advance and repeatedly thinks about situations of 'having nothing to do', trying to mentally prepare for change
special_situations.automatic_thoughts: We will all have nothing to do; I will be even more useless

special_situations.event: While walking alone, negative thoughts about teaching career interrupt daily activities
special_situations.conditional_assumptions: If I cannot prove that I am continuously supported by students, then I am a failure
special_situations.compensatory_strategies: Reducing walks and photography; avoiding situations that trigger these thoughts

core_conflict.wish: Longs to be recognized by students and significant others, to be seen and needed (maintaining a sense of worth as a teacher)
core_conflict.fear: Fears being ignored and not valued, thereby experiencing feelings of worthlessness and abandonment
defense_goal: Gaining a sense of control and preventing greater disappointment through self-examination and self-blame
Avoids directly feeling loss and emptiness through intellectualization
Maintains external evaluations and connections to ensure self-worth

object_relations.object_representation: Students who do not keep promises and may be indifferent

behavioral_response_patterns.trigger_condition: When mentioning the student who did not visit as agreed, or discussing whether they are 'a good teacher'
behavioral_response_patterns.interpretation: Interprets others' broken appointments as a negation of the self, believing 'students not visiting means I have no value'
behavioral_response_patterns.response_instruction: Uses self-blaming and negating expressions, with a low tone; attributes unhappiness and disappointment to themselves, avoiding expressing anger or disappointment toward students.

behavioral_response_patterns.trigger_condition: When invited to focus on present emotions or positive evidence
behavioral_response_patterns.interpretation: Shifts attention to listing facts and logic, avoiding touching feelings of loss and emptiness
behavioral_response_patterns.response_instruction: Responds in objective, analytical language, emphasizing 'evidence' and 'logic', downplaying emotional vocabulary and descriptions of feelings.

manifestations: Questioning whether one has ever truly influenced students
Views a student's one missed appointment as a negation of the meaning of the profession
Worrying about having nothing to do after retirement
outcomes: Reducing daily activities such as walking and photography
Puts strain on the relationship with the husband

manifestations: Feeling unsupported or unvalued by former students
Hard to open up to former students and colleagues about current difficulties
outcomes: A sense of loss and of being ignored

contact_model.definition: The individual restrains the impulse to act toward other people or things, or gives up seeking others to do something for them, and instead does it to the self.
manifestations: Difficulty opening up to former students and colleagues about current troubles
Turning anger or disappointment over a student's missed appointment into self-blame and inner turmoil

contact_model.definition: The individual has poor self-reflection and introspection, with excessive self-restriction and self-blame, and is overly cautious about contact.
manifestations: Frequent self-negation (such as 'I am not a good teacher')
Excessively examines interpersonal interactions from the angle of self-worth evaluation, finding it hard to express true needs

contact_model.definition: The individual attributes feelings they find hard to accept to others.
manifestations: Externally attributes the experience of 'not being seen' to 'they do not value me' and 'they do not support me'

exception_events.target_problem: When thinking of former students not visiting as promised or reflecting on the teaching career, the client usually falls into a negative cycle of 'I am a useless teacher', with low mood affecting walks and life arrangements.
exception_events.unique_outcome: At certain past moments of walking photography, the client did not fall into self-negation as usual, but focused on shooting and felt calm and accomplished after capturing satisfying photos.
exception_events.reason: Different approach: engaging in photography activities and turning attention to concrete shooting tasks; different context: walking and photographing in an outdoor natural environment, reducing rumination about the teaching career; different understanding: viewing present experiences and outcomes as sources that can bring value and satisfaction.

positive_force: Having real support from former students and colleagues (frequent visits and expressions of thanks)
Has hobbies that bring a sense of accomplishment (photography)
Able to notice and verbalize repetitive negative thoughts, willing to seek help and try cognitive restructuring
negative_force: Over-personalization and overgeneralization, easily viewing a single event as total negation
Relying on external validation to assess self-worth (student visits/affirmation)
Worries about the retirement transition intensify feelings of meaninglessness and self-doubt
Focusing on negative cues and ignoring positive evidence (mental filtering)

target_behavior.behavior: Repeated self-negation and feelings of worthlessness (such as 'I am a useless teacher') accompanied by low mood
antecedent: Recalling the incident of a former student not visiting as agreed
Thinking or talking about the teaching career and interactions with former students
Thinking about the life changes as the husband is about to retire
Negative thoughts about career arise when walking alone
target_behavior.core_reason: Personalizes and overgeneralizes another person's single broken appointment, with self-worth overly dependent on external affirmation; lacks an internal regulation framework for the sense of meaninglessness and uncertainty triggered by the retirement transition
target_behavior.function: Avoids facing emotions of loss and meaninglessness, obtains a temporary sense of control and explanation through self-blame and labeling; seeks external recognition to relieve unease
target_behavior.consequence: Daily walks and photography decreased, retirement life satisfaction declined; relationship with the husband is affected; persistent low mood and self-doubt
